episode.subject: greyface moray with wrasse over reef
episode.title: The next stone
episode.body:
He asked why I always went round the stones.

I said I didn't always. Went over one.

My head came down the other side. My tail was still coming up. The middle of me stayed where it was.

He waited beside me while I worked myself free.

At the next stone he went round with me.

heldDrafts.visibleScene: Greyface moray extends left across uneven reef, body bent into a shallow S curve, with patterned wrasse immediately behind. No actual straddling or stuck middle is documented.
heldDrafts.fictionBoundary: Route challenge, crossing a stone, momentary snag, waiting and changed route are fictional. No rescue or natural cooperative hunting claimed. Photograph supports nearby bodies and terrain, not sequence.
heldDrafts.continuity: If recovered with stronger image, append after I had been here anyway; preserve all eight original episodes, Anilao home, female casting and avatar. Red Sea source provenance is separate from fictional home. Pair resembles existing Still listening composition, but authored consequence is fish accommodating a different body rather than addressing wrong end.
heldDrafts.authorReview: Concrete prose trial preserved, but image quality and similar eel-followed-by-wrasse composition prevent author recommendation. Do not admit automatically; no biology claim about habitual inability to cross stones. No primary behavior source establishes the fictional snag.
